title: Return to Nature files each erased mod on its OWNER's erased pile; R262 says the erased pile follows control
summary: R262 (the owner: "All four follow control") moved the erased pile of a mod erased off a living host from mod.owner to mod.controller, and a mod's controller is its host's controller (R244). The 17-earth-b test puts the opponent's mod on P's host, runs Return to Nature, and asserts the mod lands on the OPPONENT's (owner's) pile; the 178 test's message says the same. Either Return to Nature does not go through the controller-filing path, or the test asserts superseded law. Measured by the round-1 verifier: Return to Nature groups its erased mods byOwner and files under m.owner (alreadyFiled), so a mod owned by D on a host controlled by A was filed on D's pile, while E.eraseMod files under mod.controller. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)

title: Glossary Graft row says a cached card can be grafted only under a fulfilled prophecy, omitting a live glimpse
summary: R303 (and R311) let a cached card be grafted or augmented under a live glimpse as well as a fulfilled prophecy, at the card's mana ignoring affinity. The Graft row of ui/glossary.ts says "or from cache, if a fulfilled prophecy paid for it", which omits the glimpse. Under R206 an omission is a wrong row. Fix the row's text; cite R303.

title: Return to Nature files TOKEN mods on the erased pile; R219 says a token mod erased off a living host is not filed
summary: R219: "A token mod is not filed. R133: a token is not a card, and R65's pile is a list of cards." E.eraseMod (the cost route) honours it and files nothing for a token mod. Return to Nature files its own grouped erased line for every mod it erases off hosts that stay in play, token mods included; its own comment says so. Measured by the round-1 verifier: a Wraith token mod erased by Return to Nature is recorded on the erased pile. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)

title: A graft trigger whose required target has no legal candidate still goes on the stack
summary: Designer (RAQ 1410252965276684418#2): the composite 'can't be put on the stack unless you target such unit in your bin.' The engine pushes it ('→ stack') and lets it fizzle under R86, so it can be responded to and taxed while it sits there. The no-Poison outcome matches; the mechanism does not. Low severity.
